notes: RektJackpotHook is an IMD-denominated last-buyer blitz jackpot. Constructor, in declaration order: IPoolManager manager ($poolManager), address initialOwner ($owner, which is also the immutable creator fee recipient the brief names, 0x08cd4437b077928e7fa09cf7dcdf3f7624743bd2), address launchFactory ($factory), address pairedToken (IMD, 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, the pair the request chose), address token ($token, RektToken). RektToken has no constructor arguments and mints its fixed supply to its deployer, the factory. getHookPermissions enables beforeInitialize, beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta and afterSwapReturnDelta; no liquidity or donate callbacks, so the factory's zero-liquidity fee collect passes untouched. beforeInitialize accepts only the pool manager as caller and only the launch factory as sender, binds the pool once, and requires the sorted REKTD/IMD pair, this hook, LP fee 12500 and tick spacing 60; the hook accepts the listed fee. The factory may open the pool at any valid price; initialPrice above is the reference value and the deployer derives the opening price from the policy's market cap. The hook charges 1% of gross IMD on every swap on top of the 1.25% LP fee: 50 bps to the creator recipient, paid within the same swap transaction after the router settles its input, and 50 bps to jackpotPool held as ERC-6909 IMD claims on the PoolManager. A qualifying buy of at least max(1 IMD, 5% of the pot) makes the router's caller currentLeader and sets roundEndTime to min(previous end + 120 s, now + 600 s). After expiry anyone may call settleRound, or the next swap settles: 60% of the pot to the leader, 20% transferred to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD (a source constant used only as a burn sink, not a constructor argument), 20% rolls over. Swaps are only accepted from the companion RektSwapRouter, which the hook's own constructor deploys (constructor: the same pool manager and this hook), so the launch transaction yields a tradeable pool with no later owner action; the router is not a separate manifest contract. The owner's only control, configureRouter, accepts a replacement whose runtime bytecode is identical to that router (immutables included), so it cannot change routing logic or economics. Ownership is two-step and cannot be renounced. A payout that IMD refuses to deliver (creator fee, prize or burn) is parked as a claimable balance backed by the hook's claims and anyone may retry it with claimPayout, so a refused recipient never blocks swaps or settlement. No ETH is handled: fees, prizes and burns are all IMD, and no address in this manifest is a stand-in.
